run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:41:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is driven by frontend's calls to the cart service, whose Redis/Valkey backend is unavailable because a chaos-mesh memory-stress Schedule is repeatedly applying memory stress to the valkey-cart pod, which is being OOMKilled and is now in CrashLoopBackOff with no ready endpoint. Frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts began deviating in the 5-minute window ending 07:41:41Z, exactly when the alert started, and rose from 8.89 to 563.75 per 5-minute window by 07:48:41Z. The failing frontend spans are cart-dependent operations (grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, GET/POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout), and the cart service's own server spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem show errors while cart logs repeat "Wasn't able to connect to redis". The root object is the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress, whose events show it spawning StressChaos objects every minute from 07:40:35Z that "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart". Checkout and frontend-proxy also show their own error spans in the same window, on operations that touch frontend/cart. Valkey-cart restarted 4 times with last termination OOMKilled (exit 137).

claims.text: Frontend error spans deviated at the alert start: sum by status_code of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}[5m]) was 0 for STATUS_CODE_ERROR through the window ending 07:40:41Z, then 8.888... in the window ending 07:41:41Z, climbing to 404.44 at 07:47:41Z and 563.75 at 07:48:41Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET span volume stayed roughly stable (~12k-15k per 5m) until it fell later; these are span counts, not request counts.

The frontend errors are on cart-dependent operations. Per service_name/span_name error-span increases show frontend errors on grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout; the cart service itself shows errors on POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (rising to 71.17 per 5m) and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (rising to 70.53 per 5m), and checkout shows errors on oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and HTTP POST.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (owner ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c, Deployment valkey-cart) is not ready: restartCount 4, container state waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 07:44:29Z, finishedAt 07:44:40Z. Every other otel-demo pod in the same listing was Running and ready with restartCount 0.

Deployment valkey-cart reports minimum availability lost: condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 2026-11-17T07:44:40Z, replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1. Deployment cart is unchanged at revision 1 with readyReplicas 1 / availableReplicas 1, created 07:04:01Z.

Service valkey-cart has no ready endpoint: its Endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses (100.96.5.138 on node i-0d211959f7bf532cd, targetRef pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft, port 6379); the cart service endpoint does have a ready address for pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 on port 8080.

Cart's dependency is configured as VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 in Deployment cart, and the cart container logs repeatedly emit "Wasn't able to connect to redis" interleaved with "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." (e.g. 07:47:28Z through 07:49:04Z and 07:44:40Z through 07:44:58Z).

The redis connectivity loss begins at the alert time: cart logs show "Connection to redis was restored successfully" at 07:40:53Z, then "Wasn't able to connect to redis" at 07:41:46Z, then restored again at 07:41:56Z — an intermittent pattern consistent with the ~55-second stress/recovery cycles that follow.

Chaos-mesh object otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress (kind Schedule, namespace chaos-mesh) spawned StressChaos objects each minute starting 07:40:35Z (flgz4, ckxt6, w8p5x, nt6th, 95xf6, ltcpd, v75mv, psc57). Each successful one records "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart", followed by TimeUp and Recovered about 55 seconds later; the later ones (ltcpd from 07:45:35Z, psc57 from 07:48:20Z) repeatedly record Warning Failed "no running task found: task ... not found" against the valkey-cart container IDs, and the Schedule also records Forbid "Forbid spawning new job because ... is still running".

The valkey-cart ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c gives container valkey-cart a memory limit of 10Mi (request 4Mi, CPU limit 10m), while the cart ReplicaSet cart-755465879b gives container cart a memory limit of 165Mi; both ReplicaSets are owned by their respective Deployments.

otel-demo events recorded for the valkey-cart pod include Normal Pulled/Created/Started for container valkey-cart at 07:46:13Z-07:46:15Z and a Warning BackOff at 07:48:57Z ("Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft_otel-demo").

Not every error span in the window is part of this failure: ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show a small steady error rate on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (about 1.11 per 5m) both before the alert deviation (e.g. 07:05Z-07:10Z) and during it, and frontend-proxy ingress shows small error counts (1.11-5.56 per 5m) before 07:41Z; these low pre-existing counts are background rather than evidence that those services cause the frontend alert.

Rejected: the cart service itself was redeployed or reconfigured at incident time. Deployment cart is at revision 1, created 07:04:01Z, with Ready/Available=True and 1 ready replica; its ReplicaSet cart-755465879b dates from 07:04:01Z and pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running/ready with restartCount 0, so cart's own configuration did not roll out during the window.

Hypothesis: the 10Mi memory limit on the valkey-cart container is why the injected memory stress produces OOMKilled (exit 137) restarts instead of just slow responses; even with the Schedule suspended, this very low limit makes valkey-cart likely to be killed again under normal load. Confirmation would require the valkey container's working-set/OOM metrics or a limit change observation, which were not available here.

Human follow-up: suspend or delete the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress (and its spawned StressChaos objects) so the repeated memory stress on otel-demo/valkey-cart stops; then let the valkey-cart container restart cleanly and confirm the Service endpoint returns to a ready address before validating cart and frontend recovery.

Human follow-up: review the valkey-cart container memory limit of 10Mi against valkey's real working set and raise it to a realistic value with an appropriate request, since a limit that low leaves no headroom for the cache server.

gaps: The Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and its StressChaos children could not be read directly: chaos-mesh Schedule/StressChaos kinds are not among the readable Kubernetes kinds in this Run, so the stressor's exact memory size, duration, mode and whether the Schedule is still active are known only from events.

The alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data), and a query of kube_deployment_status.* metric names also returned nothing, so the exact alert expression and deployment-level metric series are unverified in this environment.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend or cart inside 07:38Z-07:55Z (including a search for error=true), so trace-level error details and the parent-child call edges between frontend, cart and checkout are known only from span metric labels; specific error messages from spans are unavailable.

Logs of the valkey-cart container, including its previous crashed instance, could not be read (no lines returned; the API reported no previous container instance), so the OOM sequence inside valkey is not directly observed.

An otel-demo event at 07:39:29Z-07:39:30Z records FailedKillPod/Killing for pod cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz, a pod that no longer exists and whose ReplicaSet is not in the current cart Deployment (revision 1, ReplicaSet cart-755465879b); its relation to the incident is unknown, so it is not counted as impact.

Services accounting, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote and shipping were not individually checked for their own application errors or latency; no error-span series for them was returned by the per-service error query, which is not proof of health.
Whether the frontend alert has fully cleared could not be established: error spans were still present in the last returned 5-minute window ending 07:53:41Z, and the retained evidence ends at 07:54Z.
next_steps: Suspend or remove the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and confirm no StressChaos object remains active for otel-demo/valkey-cart.
Verify valkey-cart pod readiness, restart count and Service endpoints after the stress stops, and check whether the OOMKilled terminations cease.
Raise the valkey-cart container memory limit from 10Mi to a value appropriate for valkey, and re-check whether the cart 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' errors stop.
Re-check frontend error-rate span metrics after valkey-cart is ready to confirm the RequestErrorRate alert resolves.
